summary: This bill repeals the Impoundment Control Act of 1974, which currently governs how the President can propose rescissions or deferrals of budget authority.

scores.thoughts: The bill repeals the Impoundment Control Act, which currently limits the President's ability to unilaterally withhold appropriated funds. Repealing this act would give the President more power to reduce government spending by impounding funds, thus pushing towards less government spending.

By potentially allowing the President to impound funds and thus reduce government spending, the bill indirectly supports prioritizing debt reduction by limiting expenditures. This is a moderate, indirect effect on the national debt.
